why:
Perched on act-watcher at (0,0) of a 7x1 corridor with wood doors at (3,0) and (5,0). THIS SEAT EXISTS BECAUSE THE CORPUS COULD NOT RED FOUR FAULT INJECTIONS. Measured before it: zero door envelopes, zero synthesized grant, zero synthesized condition, and no scene ever reporting a SECOND sceneSeen -- session-zero's player seat carries two, but one per scene, so no visible set is ever re-compared. All four are now reached, and each was checked by actually making the change and watching this seat go red -- not by counting events.

ONE ROW ON PURPOSE. Every sight line is horizontal, so the visible set is exact by inspection instead of by tracing diagonals past a doorway: with (3,0) shut this seat sees 0,0 through 3,0; with it open, all seven. A 7x3 draft was abandoned for that reason alone. The convention this file follows says a state.json is written from the geometry with neither look() nor sight having a hand in it, and at 7x3 that was not honestly possible.

The door square (3,0) is visible while shut because sight exempts a blocker containing an endpoint of the ray. That exemption is PER BLOCKER, not a general rule, and this corridor demonstrates the difference: (5,0) is also a door and is NOT visible while (3,0) is shut, because (3,0) blocks the ray before it arrives.

THE TWO DOORS DO DIFFERENT JOBS. (3,0) gates sight. (5,0) is opened at seq 12 while still out of view, so this seat is never told; when (3,0) opens at seq 13 the far door comes into view OPEN against a belief of shut, and the projection must synthesize a doorOpened for it. That is the only synthesized door envelope in the corpus. With a single door this seat could never hold a stale belief -- it can always see (3,0) -- so the door-correction arm contributed nothing and dropping it red nothing.

act-hidden is NON-PARTY, granted at seq 7, placed at (6,0) at seq 8 and given a condition at seq 11, all of it out of this seat's sight. A party member is introduced by the roster the instant it is added, so both facts would simply forward; a non-party actor is introduced by SIGHT, so seq 13 must produce the whole introduction at once -- a synthesized actorAdded with controllers CLEARED, then its grant and its condition replayed behind it, then its placement, then a new sceneSeen. That ordering is what this seat pins.

The replayed condition carries AppliedSeq 13, the reveal, NOT the 11 at which the world applied it. A derived entry is stamped when this character learned of it. The hand-derived state.json said otherwise until the reconciliation corrected it.

Shutting (3,0) at seq 14 withdraws tok-hidden and drops the visible set back to four, which makes Visible and Explored DIFFER here -- the only place in this corpus where they do, and the distinction the plan's decision D5 turns on. (5,0) stays open for the rest of the scenario, so this seat's OpenDoors ends holding it.

THE PUNCH ALWAYS LANDS, and that is load-bearing rather than incidental. fists resolves 1d20 + brawn against footing; act-hidden has brawn 1 and footing 0, so the total is 2-21 and the hit branch is unconditional. That is what keeps the drink bump, the dazed-by-ale threshold and therefore the synthesized condition present on EVERY run, and what keeps this stream shape-stable for the drift gate. Lower the attribute or raise the defence and the golden becomes intermittent while silently dropping one of the four gaps -- the synthesized condition. Reprojected with the hit stripped, the synthesized door correction, the synthesized grant and both extra sceneSeen all survive; only the condition goes. It is the property whose absence keeps goblin-fight out of the corpus.

WHAT ONE ROW CANNOT SEE: every y here is 0, so a mutant that swapped x and y in a square key would still be caught by canSeeSquare (it would ask for "0,3", which is off the grid) but this fixture cannot distinguish a row from a column. The corpus's other scenes carry that.

This directory is also sub-project 14's ORACLE for act-watcher.
